title: Street Fighter: a fighting game movie that fans must see
summary: MANILA, Philippines – For nearly four decades since it started out as a small arcade game and eventually turned into the fighting game franchise powerhouse it is today, Capcom’s Street Fighter series…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – For nearly four decades since it started out as a small arcade game and eventually turned into the fighting game franchise powerhouse it is today, Capcom’s Street Fighter series is as universally recognizable as every iconic property and brand known in popular culture.
The series has undergone several evolutionary leaps since it started with its eponymous first title in 1987, with the most groundbreaking installment being 1991’s Street Fighter II.
That game singlehandedly made fighting games as we know it today, and helped revolutionize an entire roster of copycats and other brawlers that owe their existence to this legendary sequel.
Fast forward to 2026, and Street Fighter has become a household name.

Now in its sixth mainline installment with Street Fighter 6, the latest sequel enjoys plenty of success with fans and still features world warriors and martial artists competing in a world tournament set up to prove which of these fighters are the best of the best.

However, there is a new generation of people who may not play the games or be familiar with the series and its lore, and this is where Paramount Pictures and Legendary’s “Street Fighter” movie comes in.
As the latest attempt at adapting the IP, I can honestly tell you this is THE fighting game movie and love letter that fans and newcomers must see.

The fight begins

Directed by Japanese born American director Kitao Sakurai, Street Fighter pays homage to its fighting game roots by placing its setting directly in the early 1990’s and putting the spotlight primarily on series poster boys Ryu and Ken.

Set a few years after the end of the first World Warrior tournament, the film sees both Ansatsuken students of Master Gouken estranged and leading their own lives after a personal tragedy puts a strain on their friendship.
That time away from each other soon comes to an end as Shadaloo dictator M. Bison starts a second World Warrior tournament and calls for all the best martial artists to compete.

After being recruited by Chun-Li alongside other great fighters, Ryu and Ken must put aside their differences and fight together in order to survive Bison’s motives behind the Street Fighter tournament as a darker and even greater threat looms on the horizon.
Third strike with better results

After the disastrous release of the 1994 film starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and the even greater box office disappointment that was 2009’s Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li, all hopes in adapting a proper Street Fighter movie were crushed when the rights went into limbo and interest didn’t revive until Legendary Entertainment picked up the rights to create a film.

The past films barely adapted any of the elements that made Street Fighter what it is – powerful martial artists with an array of super powers that have become some of the most recognizable special moves known to mankind and this planet.

This movie leans into that approach hard and embraces the campiness of it all, and you will see Ryu fire and shout “HADOUKEN!” as he launches a fireball, Ken uppercutting the opponent in the air with his “SHORYUKEN!”, Chun-Li working those amazing legs and hitting a “SPINNING BIRD KICK”, and M.Bison powering up his evil energy and delivering a “PSYCHO CRUSHER”.
Beyond the special moves, almost every character in the movie lives up to the version seen in the games and the actors cast for each role fits their roles perfectly.
Andrew Koji was just born to play Ryu, and his martial arts background and past experience playing the games themselves add to his portrayal as a standout performance.
The same can be said for Noah Centineo who plays his best friend Ken Masters, with the cocky and fast living martial arts lifestyle being represented well in the young and talented actor.

Callina Liang perfectly embodies the beauty, elegance, and power needed to play Chun-Li, and she absolutely put the work and training in to transform into the self proclaimed strongest woman in the world of the Street Fighter universe.

Round up those main three cast members with supporting roles by David Dastmalchian, Mel Jarnson, rapper 50 Cent, Andrew Schultz, Olivier Richters, Eric Andre, Jason Momoa, and even WWE superstars Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns, and you have an absolute bang up roster of talents that make this a very fun movie to watch.

While it is mostly a live-action movie feature, Street Fighter includes a significant amount of anime style scenes beautifully created by Titmouse Animation that serve as flashback sequences to help with the narrative of the story.

These also serve as a direct homage to the franchise’s anime roots – especially the 1994 Street Fighter II animated movie which also placed emphasis on the relationship and story between Ryu and Ken and helped inspire the one featured in the 2026 film.

Other nods include direct references to the 1994 live-action film, as well as cameo appearances by some of very influential members of the fighting game community – including streamers Maximillian Dood, IFC Yipes, and even “Evo Moment 37” and recipient of the Daigo parry himself, Justin Wong.
Without a shadow of a doubt and just from its marketing and presentation alone, Street Fighter tops its predecessors and was made for those who love fighting games and the entire series as whole.
It’s not meant to be an Oscar level film nor should it be taken as one, and anybody who enjoys leaning into martial arts movies and video game nostalgia will have a hell of a time watching this.

It goes hand in hand with the first Mortal Kombat movie from the 90’s, and is a shining example of how to actually adapt a video game franchise and throw everything that made the games so much fun to begin with.
This is an absolute YOU WIN moment for Street Fighter fans, and I wouldn’t have it any other way. See it in the best available format possible especially on IMAX or Screen X! PERFECT!
Street Fighter is now playing in cinemas courtesy of Paramount Pictures Philippines.
